title: The Namdharis today
hookLine: they keep white dress and simple rites, and differ from most Sikhs in following a living guru

lines: A SMALL FIRE, HYMNS, A SIMPLE RITE.
A WOOL MALA IN THE HAND.
cards: A wedding in a courtyard, and everyone is in white. The men's turbans are white too, tied flat and straight across the forehead. There is no great feast of display, no long line of expensive gifts.
A small sacred fire is lit, hymns are sung, and a couple is married simply. Some guests hold a mala, a string of beads, made of white wool.
If you know Sikh weddings from photos of crimson and gold, this one may look like a different world. It belongs to the Namdharis, and today we meet them on their own terms.

teach.h: NAMDHARI: THOSE WHO HOLD TO THE NAME.
teach.b: The Namdharis are a Sikh community whose name carries naam, the Name of God, at its center: those who hold to the Name.
Year three told how the movement took shape, with Satguru Ram Singh, his call to simple living, and his stand against British rule that ended in exile.
They're also called Kukas, and tradition links that name to the cries of devotion that rose in their gatherings. Today they keep three marks.
White clothing, plain and often handspun, with the turban tied in their own straight style.
Simple rites: weddings without dowry or display, around a small fire with hymns. And a strict life of vegetarian food and daily remembrance of the Name, with the wool mala close at hand.
The wider panth holds that the line of human Gurus ended with Guru Gobind Singh, and that the Guru is now the Granth and the Khalsa together.
Namdharis follow a living guru, a line of satgurus who lead the community today. That's a real difference, and Sikhs on both sides take it seriously. This path won't argue it out.
It can listen to the Granth both sides revere.
Guru Arjan, in Raag Kanra on Ang 1299, sings, in paraphrase: no one is my enemy, and no one is a stranger; I get along with everyone.
That line doesn't erase disagreement. It sets a tone for living beside it: a difference named clearly, held honestly, and still met with respect.

how: Namdhari Sikhs wear white, tie the turban in a straight style, keep a vegetarian life with a wool mala for remembrance, marry in simple ceremonies without dowry, and follow a living satguru.

o: a group that reads scripture only in silence
a council that crowns the head of the Khalsa
a Sikh community that follows a living guru

games.q: a Namdhari friend and a Khalsa friend both come to your table. they differ on who the Guru is today. what tone does Guru Arjan's line on Ang 1299 set?
o: pick a side and argue until it's settled.
no one is an enemy, no one a stranger.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose faith or way of life differs from yours on something that matters, and say the difference to yourself once, plainly, the way they'd want it said.
Then breathe in one thing in them you can honestly respect, and breathe out, letting both stand side by side.
